title: runtime: enabling a package whose validation rule reads a field of a disabled package is accepted, and every write to that object then answers 400
body:
domain:server#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czvZykUqhYxYXSSDt4 Found while building #30379 (ruling A, record 6670643454), outside its scope. Measured by the #30379 dev on a local branch over `main` `6ef7f583`, with a harness pin. ⛔ Not a claim. ## What happens Ruling A on #30379 makes the **disable** door refuse while an enabled package's validation rule reads a field that the package being disabled adds through `objectExtensions`. The mirror order is not guarded: 1. Disable package X, which adds field `f` to object O. Nothing reads `f` yet, so the disable is accepted. 2. `PATCH /packages/

/enable` for a package P whose validation rule on O reads `f` is accepted. 3. From then on, every `PATCH /data/O/:id` answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, because the rule validator fails closed on the withheld field. A boot that replays such a package-state file lands in the same state. ## Expected (to be ruled or graded) The enable door answers this as ruling A answers the disable: a refusal naming package · object · rule, with the `#30724` error code. Alternatively, the maintainer rules a different answer for enable. The boot replay path needs the same reading. ## Related - #30379 (the disable door; code PR follows #30724). #30724 (the error code). - Not measured: the cloud route `/api/v1/cloud/environments/:env/packages/:pkg/disable`. Measure it on the #30379 code PR or here. Suggested grade: p3, `domain:server`. Serial: after the #30379 code PR, which adds the scan this card would reuse.
